Based on the healthcare Q&A matches provided, our results suggest that inhaled steroids are better than cromones in preventing admissions for asthma when two provinces with different practices for maintenance medication of steady-state asthma were compared. This indicates that inhaled steroids may be more effective in reducing hospital admission rates for asthma in children compared to cromones.

This finding is supported by the fact that our data show a significant difference in hospital admission rates between patients who received inhaled steroids and those who received cromones. Specifically, we found that inhaled steroid users had lower hospitalization rates for asthma exacerbations than cromone users.
